scr_cash_editing_a_memorized_report.purpose: Changes the saved settings of a memorized cash report — for example adding a newly opened reserve account to the month-end Cash Balances report used in owner packages.
scr_cash_editing_a_memorized_report.outcome: Standard cash reports stay complete as the portfolio's bank accounts change.
scr_cash_editing_a_memorized_report.rootCause: Memorized reports freeze their account selection. When a property opens a new trust or reserve account, the memorized report silently excludes it until someone edits it.
scr_cash_editing_a_memorized_report.ifSkipped: Owner packages omit new bank accounts and cash is understated in the package without anyone noticing.
redFlags: Memorized report account count lower than active bank accounts

scr_cash_running_a_memorized_report_or_c.purpose: Runs a memorized cash report or chart with its saved settings, adjusting only the period — the standard way to produce the monthly cash reports for the close package.
scr_cash_running_a_memorized_report_or_c.outcome: Identical, consistent cash reports every month with minimal effort.
scr_cash_running_a_memorized_report_or_c.rootCause: Owners compare month to month; running from a memorized definition guarantees the same accounts, columns and grouping each time.
scr_cash_running_a_memorized_report_or_c.ifSkipped: Reports are rebuilt ad hoc and differ between months, confusing owners.
redFlags: Period not updated before running

scr_cash_scheduling_a_memorized_report_o.purpose: Schedules a memorized cash report to run automatically — for example a daily Cash Visibility report emailed to treasury each morning or a month-end Cash Balances report stored for the package.
scr_cash_scheduling_a_memorized_report_o.outcome: Cash reports are delivered on schedule without manual runs.
scr_cash_scheduling_a_memorized_report_o.rootCause: Daily cash monitoring and month-end reporting are recurring; scheduling removes dependence on someone remembering, across offshore and onshore time zones.
scr_cash_scheduling_a_memorized_report_o.ifSkipped: Daily cash monitoring lapses and treasury decisions are made on stale balances.
redFlags: Scheduled reports emailed to former employees

scr_cash_deleting_a_memorized_report_or_.purpose: Deletes a memorized cash report or chart that is obsolete or duplicated — for example an old Cash Balances definition that still excludes the new reserve account.
scr_cash_deleting_a_memorized_report_or_.outcome: The memorized report library contains only current, approved definitions.
scr_cash_deleting_a_memorized_report_or_.rootCause: Duplicate and obsolete memorized reports lead preparers — especially new offshore staff — to run the wrong version for the owner package, producing cash figures that differ from last month's package.
scr_cash_deleting_a_memorized_report_or_.ifSkipped: Preparers pick outdated definitions and owner packages become inconsistent from month to month.
redFlags: Deleting memorized reports that have active schedules

scr_cash_edit_memorized_report_page.purpose: The page used to change a memorized cash report's name, parameters, sharing and default output.
scr_cash_edit_memorized_report_page.outcome: Memorized report definitions are maintained in one controlled place.
scr_cash_edit_memorized_report_page.rootCause: Report definitions need a clear editor so changes (accounts, filters, sharing) are deliberate and visible to the team that relies on them.
scr_cash_edit_memorized_report_page.ifSkipped: Definitions drift without anyone knowing what changed.
redFlags: Shared reports edited without notifying the team

scr_cash_schedule_memorized_report_page.purpose: The page used to set the frequency, time, recipients and output format of a scheduled memorized cash report.
scr_cash_schedule_memorized_report_page.outcome: Automated distribution of cash reports to the right people at the right time.
scr_cash_schedule_memorized_report_page.rootCause: Scheduling details (recipients, timing relative to bank feeds) decide whether a report is useful; a daily cash report sent before the bank feed imports shows yesterday's data.
scr_cash_schedule_memorized_report_page.ifSkipped: Scheduled reports go to wrong recipients or run before data is ready.
redFlags: External recipients on scheduled cash reports

scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report.purpose: Shows true available cash per property — book cash plus external balances, less holdbacks such as security deposits, outstanding payables, lender-required minimums and operating reserves — as the basis for owner distributions and funding requests.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report.outcome: A defensible figure for how much cash can be distributed to the owner or how much must be funded.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report.rootCause: Book cash overstates what is free to distribute. Institutional owners distribute excess cash monthly or quarterly and need a calculation that respects loan covenants, resident trust obligations and upcoming payables.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report.ifSkipped: Distributions are made from restricted or committed cash, leading to emergency capital calls, loan covenant breaches or trust shortfalls.
gaap: Loan agreement cash management and reserve covenants
redFlags: Available cash positive while A/P past due is large
Holdbacks not updated for the current month

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_adj.purpose: Sets the parameters — locations or groups, as-of date, holdback categories, footer text — and runs the Adjusted Available Cash report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_adj.outcome: An available cash figure scoped to the right properties and date for a distribution decision.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_adj.rootCause: The as-of date must reflect posted month-end payables and deposits; running it too early overstates available cash.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_adj.ifSkipped: Distributions are decided on a figure that excludes recent payables.
redFlags: Report run before A/P cutoff for the month

scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report_.purpose: Explains the Adjusted Available Cash columns — G/L cash, external balances, each holdback category, and the resulting available cash.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report_.outcome: Reviewers can see exactly which holdbacks reduce distributable cash and by how much.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report_.rootCause: Asset managers challenge distribution figures; column transparency lets the accountant show how each deduction was derived.
scr_cash_adjusted_available_cash_report_.ifSkipped: Distribution recommendations cannot be defended to the asset manager.
redFlags: Security deposit holdback lower than the 2110 liability

scr_cash_cash_balances_report.purpose: Shows the balance of each cash account (operating, trust, payroll, reserve, money market) and totals by property as of a date.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report.outcome: A snapshot of cash by account for the owner package and treasury monitoring.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report.rootCause: Owners and lenders look first at cash by account; restricted accounts must be distinguishable from operating cash.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report.ifSkipped: Owner packages lack account-level cash detail and restricted cash is hidden in totals.
redFlags: Negative cash balances on any account

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.purpose: Chooses accounts, locations, as-of date and grouping and runs the Cash Balances report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.outcome: Cash balances for exactly the scope requested.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.rootCause: Balances must be run as of the period end and include every cash account, or the owner package understates cash.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.ifSkipped: Balances omit accounts or use the wrong date.
redFlags: Report total not equal to cash on the balance sheet

scr_cash_cash_balances_report_columns.purpose: Explains the Cash Balances columns — account, bank, G/L balance, and totals by location.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report_columns.outcome: Correct reading of cash by account.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report_columns.rootCause: Understanding that balances are G/L (book) balances, not bank balances, avoids comparing them directly to bank statements without reconciling items.
scr_cash_cash_balances_report_columns.ifSkipped: Book balances are mistaken for bank balances in treasury decisions.
redFlags: Balances used for wires without checking outstanding checks

scr_cash_cash_analysis_report.purpose: Shows balances and activity for selected checking and savings accounts over a period — beginning balance, deposits, disbursements, transfers and ending balance.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report.outcome: A cash roll-forward per account explaining how cash moved in the period.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report.rootCause: Asset managers ask why cash dropped or rose; a roll-forward by account answers it and supports the cash flow statement.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report.ifSkipped: Cash movements cannot be explained quickly to the owner.
redFlags: Ending balance not equal to next period's beginning balance

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.purpose: Selects the checking and savings accounts, the period and footer text, then runs the Cash Analysis report to produce a cash roll-forward for the owner package or an asset manager question.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.outcome: A cash roll-forward for exactly the accounts and period being asked about.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.rootCause: The roll-forward only ties to the balance sheet if every relevant account (including trust and reserve accounts) and the exact period are selected; leaving one out produces a roll-forward that does not explain the balance change.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.ifSkipped: Roll-forwards omit accounts and the asset manager's question about the cash movement cannot be answered.
redFlags: Period spanning closed and open periods without a note

scr_cash_cash_analysis_report_columns.purpose: Explains the Cash Analysis columns — beginning balance, receipts, disbursements, transfers in and out, and ending balance per account.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report_columns.outcome: Correct interpretation of cash movement components.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report_columns.rootCause: Distinguishing transfers from operating receipts and disbursements matters for the cash flow statement.
scr_cash_cash_analysis_report_columns.ifSkipped: Transfers are mistaken for operating inflows or outflows.
redFlags: Transfers classified as operating activity

scr_cash_pc_cards_report.purpose: Lists all issued and cancelled petty cash debit cards with holder, property, limit, status and balance.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report.outcome: An inventory of the petty cash card program for oversight and audit.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report.rootCause: Every card is spending authority; auditors and regional managers need the full list to confirm cards match current staff and policy limits.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report.ifSkipped: Cards held by departed staff or with excessive limits go unnoticed.
redFlags: Active cards for terminated employees
Limits above policy

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.purpose: Sets filters (card status, property, holder) and runs the PC Cards report — typically all active cards for a region — to support the quarterly access review of petty cash cards.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.outcome: A targeted card inventory to compare against current site staff rosters.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.rootCause: Quarterly access reviews require matching every active card to a current employee. Filtering by property and status gives regional managers a list they can actually verify.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.ifSkipped: Access reviews are skipped or incomplete, and cards held by departed staff stay active.
redFlags: No access review evidence for the quarter

scr_cash_pc_cards_report_columns.purpose: Defines the PC Cards report columns — card ID, holder, property, status, limit and balance.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report_columns.outcome: Correct reading of the card inventory.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report_columns.rootCause: Card ID and status columns are needed to match cards to holders and confirm cancellations took effect.
scr_cash_pc_cards_report_columns.ifSkipped: Cancelled cards not confirmed as cancelled.
redFlags: Status 'active' for cards reported lost

scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report.purpose: Lists petty cash card transactions across cards and properties with merchant, amount, date, status and coding.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report.outcome: Transaction-level visibility of card spending for review and audit.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report.rootCause: Misuse shows up in transaction patterns (personal merchants, split purchases, weekend spending) that only a transaction report reveals.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report.ifSkipped: Card misuse goes undetected until a large loss or an audit finding.
redFlags: Personal merchants
Transactions just under limits

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.purpose: Sets parameters (date range, cards, status) and runs the PC Card Transactions report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.outcome: A focused list of card transactions for a review period.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.rootCause: Monthly card reviews need transactions for one period and property; broad reports hide issues in volume.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.ifSkipped: Reviews are too broad to be effective and misuse hides in the volume.
redFlags: Open (unsubmitted) transactions older than 30 days

scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report_col.purpose: Defines the PC Card Transactions columns — card ID, merchant, amount, date, status and GL coding.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report_col.outcome: Correct interpretation of card transaction detail.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report_col.rootCause: Status and coding columns reveal which spending has been accounted for and which has not.
scr_cash_pc_card_transactions_report_col.ifSkipped: Unaccounted spending is misread as submitted.
redFlags: Transactions with no coding

scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report.purpose: Lists petty cash cards that were billed — program fees charged per card — for allocation to properties.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report.outcome: Card program fees are charged to the properties that hold cards.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report.rootCause: Card programs carry per-card fees; allocating them correctly keeps each owner paying only for its own cards.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report.ifSkipped: Program fees sit in a corporate account or are charged to the wrong owner.
redFlags: Fees billed for cancelled cards

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.purpose: Selects the billing period and properties and runs the PC Cards Billing report to list per-card program fees for the period before they are allocated to properties.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.outcome: A billing list for the period's card fees that can be checked against the program provider's invoice.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.rootCause: Program fees must be verified against the provider's invoice before being paid and allocated; the billing report is the independent count of billable cards.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_pc_.ifSkipped: Card program invoices are paid without verification, including fees for cancelled cards.
redFlags: Report totals not matching the program invoice

scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report_columns.purpose: Defines the PC Cards Billing columns — system card ID, property, billing period and fee — used to allocate card program fees to the owners whose sites hold the cards.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report_columns.outcome: Card program fees are charged to the correct property and owner.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report_columns.rootCause: Management companies pay the card program centrally but must charge each owner only for its own cards. The property and card ID columns drive that allocation.
scr_cash_pc_cards_billing_report_columns.ifSkipped: Fees are allocated to the wrong properties, and owners pay for cards at sites they do not own.
redFlags: Cards without property assignment

scr_cash_cash_visibility_report.purpose: Compares G/L bank balances with the latest bank-reported balances from bank feeds for each account, highlighting differences.
scr_cash_cash_visibility_report.outcome: Daily early warning of cash differences — unrecorded debits, fraud, or unrecorded deposits — before month-end.
scr_cash_cash_visibility_report.rootCause: Waiting for month-end recs means unauthorized debits can go unnoticed for weeks. Comparing book to bank daily catches them within the NACHA return window.
scr_cash_cash_visibility_report.ifSkipped: Unauthorized ACH debits are found after the 60-day return window closes and the loss becomes unrecoverable.
redFlags: Persistent unexplained differences on an account

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.purpose: Chooses the bank accounts and comparison options and runs the Cash Visibility report, usually each morning after bank feeds import, to compare G/L cash with bank-reported balances.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.outcome: A daily book-versus-bank comparison for the monitored accounts.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.rootCause: Treasury runs this daily for high-risk accounts (operating accounts that receive resident ACH and pay vendors). The parameters decide which accounts are watched, so a missed account is simply not monitored.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cas.ifSkipped: High-risk accounts are not monitored daily and unauthorized debits are discovered weeks later.
redFlags: Accounts with feeds excluded from monitoring

scr_cash_cash_visibility_report_columns.purpose: Explains the Cash Visibility columns, which vary by comparison option — G/L balance, bank balance, difference and feed date.
scr_cash_cash_visibility_report_columns.rootCause: The feed date column shows whether the bank balance is current; stale feeds make differences meaningless.
scr_cash_cash_visibility_report_columns.ifSkipped: Stale feed data is mistaken for real differences.
redFlags: Feed dates more than a day old

scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.purpose: Summarizes bank transactions (from feeds or imports) by account and type — deposits, checks, ACH debits, fees — for a period.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.outcome: A view of bank-side activity by type, useful for spotting unusual debits or fee spikes.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.rootCause: Summarizing bank activity by type highlights anomalies (a new ACH originator debiting the account, a jump in fees) that line-level matching can miss.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.ifSkipped: Unusual bank activity patterns go unnoticed.
redFlags: New ACH debit originators

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.purpose: Selects bank accounts and a period and runs the Bank Transactions Summary report, which totals bank-side activity by transaction type for treasury review.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.outcome: Bank activity summarized by type for the review period, ready for the monthly treasury check.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.rootCause: Periodic review of bank activity by type is a treasury control that complements reconciliations: a new ACH originator or a spike in returned items is easier to see in a summary than line by line.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.ifSkipped: The treasury review is not performed and unusual bank activity patterns go unnoticed.
redFlags: Summary not reviewed monthly

scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.purpose: Defines the Bank Transactions Summary columns — account, transaction type (deposit, check, ACH debit, ACH credit, fee, return), count and total — for reading bank activity patterns.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.outcome: Correct reading of bank activity by type and volume.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.rootCause: Counts by type reveal volume anomalies: a sudden rise in ACH debits or returned items is an early fraud or process-failure signal that totals alone can hide.
scr_cash_bank_transactions_summary_repor.ifSkipped: Volume anomalies such as new unauthorized ACH debits are missed.
redFlags: Unexplained increases in debit counts

scr_cash_bank_register_report.purpose: Lists every book transaction affecting a bank account — checks, deposits, transfers, fees, JEs — in detail or summary mode for a period.
scr_cash_bank_register_report.outcome: The book-side register of cash activity, used for reconciliation support and audit.
scr_cash_bank_register_report.rootCause: Auditors and reviewers test cash activity from the bank register; it also shows JEs posted directly to cash, which bypass normal controls.
scr_cash_bank_register_report.ifSkipped: Cash activity cannot be reviewed in one place and direct JEs to cash go unnoticed.
redFlags: Manual JEs to cash accounts

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.purpose: Chooses bank accounts, date range and detail or summary mode and runs the Bank Register report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.outcome: A bank register for the requested accounts and period.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.rootCause: Detail mode is needed for reconciliation support; summary mode suits monthly review of activity totals.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_ban.ifSkipped: The wrong level of detail is produced for the purpose.
redFlags: Register period different from the reconciliation period

scr_cash_bank_register_report_columns.purpose: Defines the Bank Register columns — date, type, reference, payee or payer, amount and running balance.
scr_cash_bank_register_report_columns.rootCause: Transaction type and reference columns let reviewers separate routine activity from unusual entries such as manual JEs posted directly to cash.
scr_cash_bank_register_report_columns.ifSkipped: Unusual entries to cash are not spotted during review.
redFlags: Entries without references

scr_cash_check_register_report.purpose: Lists vendor payments (checks and electronic) by bank account with payee, number, date, amount and status (outstanding, cleared, voided).
scr_cash_check_register_report.outcome: A disbursement register for payment review, reconciliation and audit sampling.
scr_cash_check_register_report.rootCause: Disbursements are a primary fraud area; reviewers scan the check register for unusual payees, sequence gaps and duplicate amounts.
scr_cash_check_register_report.ifSkipped: Unusual payments and sequence gaps go unreviewed.
redFlags: Gaps in check sequence
Payees not in the vendor master

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_che.purpose: Chooses bank accounts, date range, payment types and status and runs the Check Register report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_che.outcome: A disbursement register scoped to the review.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_che.rootCause: Reviews and audits need registers for specific accounts and periods; the right filters keep them focused.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_che.ifSkipped: Registers are too broad or miss payment types.
redFlags: Electronic payments excluded from review

scr_cash_check_register_report_columns.purpose: Defines the Check Register columns — bank, payment number, date, payee, amount, status and cleared date.
scr_cash_check_register_report_columns.outcome: Correct reading of payment status for reconciliation and escheat review.
scr_cash_check_register_report_columns.rootCause: The cleared date and status columns identify stale outstanding checks that need follow-up or escheatment.
scr_cash_check_register_report_columns.ifSkipped: Stale checks are not identified and escheat deadlines pass.
redFlags: Outstanding checks older than 180 days

scr_cash_deposits_register_report.purpose: Lists deposits by bank and date with their totals and contents, supporting the deposit side of the bank reconciliation.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report.outcome: A deposits register used to match deposits in transit and investigate missing deposits.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report.rootCause: Site-level cash misappropriation often shows up as late or missing deposits; the register lets reviewers check deposit timing and completeness.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report.ifSkipped: Late or missing site deposits go unnoticed, and so does possible skimming.
redFlags: Gaps of several days between deposits at an active property

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_dep.purpose: Chooses the bank account, period and detail level and runs the Deposits Register report, typically per property per month to review deposit frequency and completeness.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_dep.outcome: A deposits register scoped to the review period.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_dep.rootCause: Deposit reviews are done by property and month so that gaps in deposit frequency at a specific leasing office stand out; portfolio-wide output buries them.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_dep.ifSkipped: Deposit reviews are unfocused or skipped.
redFlags: Register not tied to bank credits
